Project Overview

We are hiring a postdoctoral researcher for a funded, teen-centered project focused on AI safety and youth digital well-being. The project designs and evaluates empowerment-oriented mobile tools that do not rely on monitoring or enforcement, supporting healthier teen–mobile technology relationships.

The work is animated by a few guiding questions: What would digital interventions look like if designed to facilitate care rather than optimize engagement? Whose definition of “safety” are we designing toward—and what would it mean to treat teens as genuine partners in defining it? How might teens’ shared experiences of platform life become a resource for critical reflection, rather than data to be acted upon by adults?

The postdoctoral researcher will lead the end-to-end research and development cycle, from mixed-method empirical grounding (e.g., cultural probes, interviews/focus groups, and co-design) to translating findings into design requirements, iteratively prototyping a mobile app system, and conducting a real-world deployment and evaluation with teen participants. The role involves close collaboration with faculty, students, and community/nonprofit partners in Singapore and, as needed, coordinating with a developer and UX designer to ensure technical feasibility and the responsible integration of AI-related features. Expected outcomes include a deployable research prototype, rigorous evidence of empowerment and reflective engagement, and publications in top-tier HCI/CSCW venues.

Required Qualifications

Applicants must have:

• A PhD (completed by the start date preferred*) in a relevant field, such as HCI, CSCW, Information Science, Interaction Design, Computer Science (human-centered), Digital Health, STS, or related areas
• An active publication record in leading HCI/CSCW venues and/or related journals
• Demonstrated ability to lead end-to-end research projects with strong project management and collaboration skills
• Strong qualitative and design research capability (study design, fieldwork, analysis, synthesis into system requirements)
• Demonstrated prototyping ability, including rapid iteration toward mid- to high-fidelity mobile prototypes (or equivalent evidence of deployed interactive systems)

Preferred Qualifications

• Background in Human–AI interaction, AI safety/responsible AI, algorithmic experience, or sociotechnical systems research
• Ability to design and deploy mobile app prototypes (Android/iOS or cross-platform), especially for field studies
• Familiarity with teen/adolescent mental health, youth digital well-being, online safety, or school/community-based research
• Participatory design experience with youth and/or community partners; experience navigating ethics for adolescent research

Why NUS

NUS is a leading global university with strong interdisciplinary strengths across computing, design, and the social sciences. This role offers an opportunity to drive a high-impact project with a strong publication pipeline, close mentorship, and collaboration across research and community partners.

Why Singapore

Singapore is an ideal context for teen digital well-being and online safety research: it is highly connected, mobile-first, and supported by active national initiatives focused on safe and meaningful digital participation. The ecosystem includes schools, youth organizations, and public agencies that enable rigorous, culturally grounded field research and translation to practice.
